title: Finite pushforward of module assertions
statement: Let k be algebraically closed, Λ a commutative ring, g:Y → Spec k a separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], f:X → Y finite, and F an étale sheaf of Λ-modules on X. If the eight conditional assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], with module constructibility [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], hold for (f ≫ g,F), they hold for (g,f_*F). No torsion hypothesis on F or Noetherian hypothesis on Λ is imposed.

proof.text: The finite-stalk product formula identifies the counit on each geometric stalk as a split product projection. Geometric points jointly reflect epimorphisms, so the module counit is epi. Source primary torsion and torsion of invertible order follow by lifting a stalk element through the counit and transporting annihilators along upperStarCompSheafFiberIso.

Use the bijective finite cohomology edge map for the underlying abelian sheaf. Forgetting module coefficients commutes definitionally with direct image. Transfer C1, C2, C3 by injectivity into subsingleton source cohomology, using finite-over-affine for C2 and the primary-torsion reflection for C3.

Reflect module constructibility using the strict coefficient lemma, and invertible-order torsion using the counit. Transfer finiteness through the injective edge equivalence for C4 and C5. Finite over proper is proper for C5.

For C6 and C7, take the pullback of f along the field-extension source map and paste its cartesian square with the given square over k. Finite exchange and both finite edge maps are bijective, and the edge base-change identity gives a commuting comparison square. Bijectivity of the source pullback is equivalent to bijectivity of the target pullback. For C6 use invertible-order reflection; for C7 use properness of f composed with g.

For C8 pull back any open immersion into Y to X; it remains open. The same finite-exchange/edge square identifies surjectivity of the two restrictions. Apply C8 on X and assemble the eight separate clauses using assertions_iff.
